answers: Connor Cummins' family describes him to WABC-TV as a photography devotee—and that enthusiasm may have cost him his life. The New Jersey man, said to be either 20 or 24 years old, and an 18-year-old pal ascended the scaffolding outside NYC's Four Seasons hotel Wednesday night in search of the perfect panoramic picture—but Cummins may have slipped on railings made slippery by the rain and fell nine stories to his death, cops tell NJ.com. An NYPD spokesman tells the New York Daily News that the initial investigation suggests the men weren't guests of the hotel. Cummins, who originally hails from Rockaway and whose Facebook page indicates he's now a student at the University of Massachusetts Amherst, per ABC, landed on one of the hotel's lower-level rooftops around 11:15pm and was pronounced dead at the scene, reports the New York Post. His friend wasn't injured and was questioned by authorities to fill in the blanks; he was released Thursday morning without being charged. "He was a loving boy, that's all I can say," one of Cummins' relatives tells the Post. "I don't know what happened." (There's more suspicion surrounding a Muslim teen's fatal fall off a Seattle building.)

full.prediction:
**Summary of the Four Seasons Hotel Tragedy**

On Wednesday, a tragic incident occurred at the 52-story Four Seasons Hotel in Manhattan, resulting in the death of 20-year-old Connor Cummings of Rockaway, New Jersey. Cummings and his 18-year-old friend, Dimitri Olivares, were attempting to take photographs from the hotel’s rooftop when the accident took place. According to multiple news reports, the two young men climbed scaffolding located in an interior shaft of the hotel on 57th Street. 

Cummings, who was a sophomore psychology major at the University of Massachusetts Amherst and also a photography student, was reportedly on his way to the roof when he slipped and fell nine stories. The fall occurred around 11:15 p.m. in the pouring rain, and Cummings landed on a 43rd-floor landing before being pronounced dead at the scene. Olivares, who was identified as the friend, climbed down to seek help and later called hotel security after fleeing the scene in a taxi. He was later interviewed by police and released without charges.

The incident took place on the hotel’s restricted rooftop, which is not open to the public. The pair had accessed the area using the hotel’s elevator and climbed stairs to reach the rooftop. While there, they climbed a ladder to get a panoramic view of the city skyline. Cummings lost his footing while walking backward on a metal catwalk and fell approximately 25 feet. 

Hotel officials stated that the safety and security of guests, patrons, and employees is a top priority and that they are cooperating with the ongoing investigation. Police have not yet filed charges against Olivares, though his family expressed concern over the circumstances of the incident, noting that Cummings was a “good kid” who was not drinking and had no history of risky behavior.

Cummings was described by friends and family as a passionate photographer, a dedicated student, and a caring individual who was always willing to help others. His fraternity brothers at the University of Massachusetts Amherst posted a heartfelt message on Facebook mourning his death and highlighting his “fiery passion” for photography. A childhood friend from New Jersey also expressed deep sorrow, calling Cummings a remarkable person who lived with integrity and kindness.

The incident has sparked discussions about safety on private property and the risks associated with unauthorized access to restricted areas. As the investigation continues, the community mourns the loss of a young man with a bright future and a deep love for his craft.
